provenance.contract: This file ships ONLY question sets we author ourselves. A real funder's question set is external fact — the exact wording of a question and the exact character limit on its field — and neither can be recalled, inferred or approximated. Getting a limit wrong produces an answer that will not paste, which is a worse failure than having no set at all.
provenance.how_to_add_a_real_funder: Open the funder's own published question list or guidance, transcribe each question verbatim with its stated limit, record the source_url, then insert the row with status='unverified'. An operator promotes it to status='open' with next_review 90 days out only after a second read against the funder's current guidance — in the database, not here.
provenance.warning: Do not add a funder's questions from memory. Do not estimate a character limit. Verification is an act somebody performs, not a value somebody types.

question_sets.name: Expression of interest (generic)
question_sets.notes: Our own product template, not a transcription of any funder's form. It exists so the answer sheet is usable on day one and so a consultant has somewhere to start before a real set is curated. The limits are our defaults, chosen to sit inside the ranges UK funders commonly use — check them against the actual form before submitting anything.

questions.text: In one sentence, what is the project?
questions.guidance: Assessors read this first and skim the rest. Name the place, the thing being built or saved, and who it is for.

questions.text: Who is the applicant organisation, and what is its legal form?
questions.guidance: Registered name, number and structure. Say when it was formed and what it exists to do.

questions.text: What need does this project address, and how do you know?
questions.guidance: Evidence, not assertion. Cite the survey, the waiting list, the census figure or the consultation that establishes the need.

questions.text: What will the funding pay for?
questions.guidance: Specific costs against specific activities. Refer to the budget rather than repeating every line of it.

questions.text: What is the full funding stack, and what is already secured?
questions.guidance: Be explicit about what is confirmed, what is applied for, and what is still a gap. Funders check.

questions.text: How is the community involved in this project?
questions.guidance: Governance, not consultation. Who decides, and how did they come to be the deciders?

questions.text: What are the main risks, and how are they being managed?
questions.guidance: Name real risks with real mitigations. A risk register with nothing above 'medium' reads as unexamined.

questions.text: What will have changed if this project succeeds, and how will you know?
questions.guidance: Outcomes with measures against them. Say what you will count and when you will count it.
